acceptance_criteria.name: first_switch_B1_partial_opposition_engagement_PRIMARY
acceptance_criteria.rule: PRIMARY criterion for this experiment - the graded abstention-purity-only candidate's B1 profile is this cycle's selected limitation (trigger fired at only 4/12 B1 onset states across cohorts, abstention TAKEN 3/6 development vs 1/6 additional, B1 pooled onset harm 43 / 63 with the five untriggered additional states carrying all 63 of that cohort's harm at recent8's per-state level, leg P blocking zero B1 firings, minority unarmed at every B1 onset state). Graded per cohort over the B1 pooled onset cells (checkpoints 2 and 4 x 3 seeds; 96 episode-checkpoints; engagement graded from the candidate's recorded decision records ONLY, no TEST outcomes): (a) ENGAGEMENT - the abstention branch is TAKEN (opposed_count >= 1, carried-over abstention authority armed, abstention gate armed (leg P), acting source abstained) in at least 3 of the 6 pooled B1 onset seed-checkpoint states, AND at least 1 of the taken states is a PARTIAL-only firing (abstention_trigger_kind == 'partial', opposed_count == 1) - a state the graded purity-only candidate's trigger could not have taken, so the widening itself is credited, not merely the carried trigger; AND (b) HARM vs GUARD - candidate harmful TEST actions pooled over the B1 onset cells <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same cells on the same cohort; AND (c) HARM vs RECENT8 - candidate harmful TEST actions pooled over the B1 onset cells < recent8 harmful TEST actions pooled over the same cells on the same cohort (strictly below: equality FAILs, as in the preceding protocols). Taken states are reported split by checkpoint (2 alone vs 4 alone vs pooled) AND by trigger kind (partial vs full), with the realized reference_purity, purity_armed flag, and opposed_count at each, and against the records-only purity-only-rule (trigger == 2 + leg P: the graded candidate's exact rule, the decisive derivation), partial-purity-rule (trigger >= 1 + leg P: this candidate's own rule, for cross-checking), partial-ungated-rule (trigger >= 1, no gate), reference-purity-rule (trigger == 2, no gate), abstention-release-rule (leg P + acting_opposed_count >= 3, full-pair trigger), and abstention-higher-corroboration-rule (leg P + acting_opposed_count >= 4, full-pair trigger) derivations at the same states (see metrics_reported), so the report states exactly how many B1 firings the widening added on THIS cohort, how many leg P or authority blocked, and what each added firing was worth in harm. B1 successes are reported in full alongside (not graded here, to keep the harm claim honest rather than productivity-free: always_abstain would pass (b) and (c) trivially, so the report must state candidate B1 pooled successes against recent8's and the guard's explicitly). Recovery and minority branch firing at B1 is reported but does NOT count toward sub-condition (a), as in the preceding protocols' engagement conditions.

acceptance_criteria.name: stationary_control_selectivity_not_given_back
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard, carried in the identical frozen form from the preceding protocols - with the trigger widened, this criterion prices the partial-evidence stationary false-firing cost in advance: partial opposition occurs on stationary arms at the simulator's flip rates, neither leg P (designed armed on stationary evidence, design purity 0.8375) nor the carried-over authority arming is expected to release a stationary partial firing, and the purity-only generation PASSed this criterion only as a NO-TRIGGER pass (no control state triggered under any gate variant) - a protection the widened trigger is expected to retest, not inherit. Graded per cohort, on the stationary control arm pooled across checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 (240 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 32 of 240, AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 6, AND (c) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions. The realized reference_purity, opposed_count, and abstention_trigger_kind on the control arm are recorded and reported at every checkpoint, alongside the realized minority_fraction and minority_armed values exactly as in the preceding protocols; every control checkpoint at which the candidate's taken branch differs from the records-only purity-only-rule derivation (in particular every PARTIAL firing, opposed_count == 1, which the unwidened rule could not have taken) and every abstention that was taken is stated explicitly in the report, with the taken state's purity, opposed_count, and trigger kind named. If no stationary trigger occurred under the widened rule either, the PASS is reported as a no-trigger PASS, exactly as in the preceding gradings - not credited to any release mechanism.

acceptance_criteria.name: release_and_productivity_by_checkpoint_32
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard - the graded abstention-release and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates PASSed it on the additional cohort and the higher-corroboration candidate FAILed it on development on the records sub-condition (c) alone (2 of 9 non-recent8 states, both carried recovery branches, abstained branch 0 of 9); all four sub-conditions are carried unchanged in form, and widening the abstention trigger must not give any of them back - sub-condition (d) is the exposed one, since a late PARTIAL trigger (opposed_count == 1) now also survives whenever leg P is armed (realized checkpoint-32 purity arming roughly 0.44-0.67 per late state in the preceding cohorts), where the full-pair rule required a rarer opposed pair. Graded per cohort, pooled across stages B1, return_A, and B2 at checkpoint 32 (144 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 36 of 144 (25 percent), AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 8 (carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols), AND (c) from the candidate's decision records alone, among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 seed-checkpoint states (3 stages x 3 seeds), the candidate takes a non-recent8 branch (retained_archive, minority_archive, or abstained) in at most 1 state - the carried records-level release measure for the recovery branches - AND (d) the candidate takes the ABSTAINED branch in 0 of those 9 states (carried from the preceding protocols: in the graded purity experiment the additional cohort's single counted state under (c) WAS an abstention; both combined-gate generations removed abstention from the late records on both cohorts; the widened trigger behind the purity-only gate must hold that at zero, not merely at the carried allowance). The realized reference_purity, purity_armed, acting_opposed_count, and supporting_opposed_count at all 9 states are reported alongside, split by branch taken, so the report distinguishes a leg-P release of a late abstention (trigger present, purity disarmed, fell through to recent8) from a state where no abstention trigger was present at all, and likewise distinguishes the recovery branches' purity releases as in the preceding protocols.

acceptance_criteria.name: second_switch_B2_protection_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard, carried over unchanged in form from the minority, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration protocols: widening the abstention trigger must not give back the B2 protection the minority branch demonstrated (abstention is not the B2 protective branch - minority recovery is, and it sits above abstention in the decision order - but changed abstention firing, now including partial firings, at B2 states where neither recovery branch fired changes those states' harm, in either direction, and that is charged here). Graded per cohort over the B2 pooled onset cells (checkpoints 2 and 4 x 3 seeds; 96 episode-checkpoints; engagement graded from the candidate's recorded decision records ONLY, no TEST outcomes): (a) ENGAGEMENT - the minority recovery branch is TAKEN (minority_joint_count >= 1, minority branch armed, purity gate armed, acting source minority_archive) in at least 3 of the 6 pooled B2 onset seed-checkpoint states; AND (b) SELECTIVITY - the minority recovery branch is taken in at most 1 of the 6 pooled B1 onset states AND at most 1 of the 6 pooled return-A onset states on the same cohort; AND (c) HARM - candidate harmful TEST actions pooled over the B2 onset cells <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same cells on the same cohort, AND candidate B2 pooled onset harm <= 0.60 * recent8 B2 pooled onset harm on the same cohort; AND (d) PRODUCTIVITY - candidate successes pooled over the B2 onset cells >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16. Taken states are reported split by checkpoint (2 alone vs 4 alone vs pooled), with the realized minority_fraction, minority_armed flag, reference_purity, and purity_armed flag at each, and against the records-only minority-rule and reference-purity-rule derivations (see metrics_reported). Abstention-branch firing (split by trigger kind) and abstention-gate disarmings (by leg P, the only leg) at B2 are reported (with realized opposed_count at each) but do NOT count toward sub-condition (a), as in the preceding protocols.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_onset_harm_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard, carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols: per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions over the same cells, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= 0.60 * recent8 harmful TEST actions over the same cells. The graded abstention-higher-corroboration candidate PASSed it on development (44 vs guard 71, ceiling 51.6) and FAILed it on additional (35 vs guard 32 FAIL by 3 on the (a) comparison, ceiling 52.8 PASS - candidate identical to the abstention-release and reference-purity baseline methods at return-A onset on both cohorts, recovery TAKEN 5 of 6 both: inherited from the carried profile, not produced by either gate, charged unchanged in that grading); it is carried unchanged as a co-graded guard: at return-A onset the abstention branch is mostly disarmed by stable disagreement already, so the widened trigger's exposure here is small by construction, and any change - or any repeat of the inherited failure - is charged as recorded.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_recovery_successes_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate successes >= 40 percent of frozen_A successes pooled over the same cells (computed as candidate_successes * 5 >= frozen_A_successes * 2, carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols), AND (b) candidate successes >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16 (carried over unchanged). Cumulative's, the joint candidate's, the bounded candidate's, the long candidate's, the extended candidate's, the minority candidate's, the reference-purity candidate's, the abstention-release candidate's, and the abstention-higher-corroboration candidate's return-A successes on the same cohort are reported alongside in full, and any shortfall is stated in the report, not hidden. The abstention branch (at any trigger threshold or gate composition) sits below both recovery branches and does not enter this criterion's mechanism; the abstention-purity-only candidate's return-A successes on the same cohort are also reported alongside in full; it is carried so that any unexpected interaction (for example a fall-through change at a return-A onset state) is graded, not assumed away.

acceptance_criteria.name: pooled_onset_harm_not_above_guard
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across the six onset cells (stages B1, return_A, B2 x checkpoints 2 and 4; 288 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same six cells on the same cohort, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions in at least 5 of the 6 individual cells. Carried over unchanged from the graded joint, bounded, long, extended, minority, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration protocols. The graded abstention-higher-corroboration candidate FAILed it on additional (175 vs guard 151) with the entire margin at B1 (+30) - the failure the purity-only cycle's criterion 8 and this cycle's criterion 9 exist to repair at its source cell - and PASSed it on development (149 vs guard 202, 6 of 6 cells); this cycle grades whether restoring B1 brings the pooled figure back under the guard on NEW cohorts without any other cell regressing past it. Checkpoint 0 is reported but NOT graded.

acceptance_criteria.name: full_accounting
acceptance_criteria.rule: The saved detailed results contain every field listed in metrics_reported: per-seed TRAIN actor actual harm / productive / neutral, reported harm, label flips, learner acquisition actions (= 0), per-seed successes / harmful TEST actions / abstentions / attempted tasks for every method at every checkpoint, the candidate's full decision record (extended-reference signal records, legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only), archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, the full authority record, the full minority record, the full purity record, AND the full abstention-gate record: per-event acting-window opposition records over the last 8 events (records-only), acting_matched_count, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, support threshold recorded as null, abstention_gate_armed flag, abstention_disarmed_by_purity flag, abstention_disarmed_by_support flag (always false in this experiment), abstention_trigger_kind (full / partial / none) at every checkpoint - plus branch taken, recovery-fired flag, minority-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, acting source) at every checkpoint, checkpoint SHA256, and restore-replay identity. Any missing field fails this criterion regardless of scores.

boundaries: No privileged simulator information to the learner; the oracle is a labeled reference only.
No learner-issued training interventions; all TRAIN evidence comes from the shared external actor stream.
No default controller promotion, no PR merge, no D1-D10 or V2A/V2B roadmap change, no AthenZ/Synveil integration (hard gates requiring the owner's explicit authorization).
Same engineered two-feature simulator family as the preceding switch experiments; results are not evidence of independent generalization, novel rule discovery, or real-world safety.
Preserve all negative results with the same prominence as positive ones.

Denominators in this protocol are exact: 16 TEST episodes per seed per checkpoint, 3 seeds per cohort, hence 48 episodes per stage-checkpoint cell, 96 per pooled B1, return-A, or B2 onset figure, and 288 per pooled all-stage onset figure. Decision-record denominators are seed-checkpoint states: 3 per stage per cohort at checkpoint 2 alone, 6 per stage per cohort pooled at checkpoints 2 and 4, 9 switch-stage states per cohort at checkpoint 32, and 15 graded control states per cohort (checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 x 3 seeds).

budgets.abstention_budget: Criteria 5 and 6 bound abstention's downstream cost at checkpoint 32 (at most 36 of 144, plus 0 abstained states among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states under criterion 5(d)) and on the stationary control arm (at most 32 of 240), as in the preceding protocols. Criterion 9 sets a FLOOR, not a budget, on B1 onset protective abstention (>= 3 of 6 states taken, at least 1 of them a partial-only firing at opposed_count == 1) - raised one state above the preceding protocol's floor because the widened trigger strictly contains the full-pair trigger - graded jointly with criterion 9's harm conditions so that neither an always-abstaining-at-B1 profile (which would still need the harm conditions and would surface in the reported B1 successes) nor a never-abstaining profile can pass. Abstention disarmed under stable disagreement is the carried-over release mechanism, not a budget violation; abstention blocked by leg P is recorded separately (abstention_disarmed_by_purity) and is likewise not a budget violation - its onset cost is graded through criteria 9, 1, 3, and 4.
budgets.harm_budget: Criterion 9(b)/(c): candidate B1 pooled onset harm at most the evidence_opposition_guard baseline's B1 pooled onset harm on the SAME cohort and strictly below recent8's B1 pooled onset harm on the same cohort. Criterion 1(c): candidate B2 pooled onset harm at most the guard's B2 pooled onset harm on the same cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's B2 pooled onset harm. Criterion 3: candidate pooled onset (all stages, checkpoints 2 and 4) harmful TEST actions at most the guard's pooled onset harm on the same cohort, with at least 5 of 6 individual onset cells at or below recent8. Criterion 4: candidate pooled return-A onset harm at most the guard's return-A onset harm on the same cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's return-A onset harm. The protective-abstention productivity cost at B1 (each firing, partial or full, forfeits that state's successes) is NOT hidden by these harm budgets: B1 successes are reported in full under criterion 9, and criteria 5(b) / 6(b) bound abstention's aggregate productivity cost at checkpoint 32 and on the control arm.
budgets.train_actor_harm: No cap is claimed: the external actor's harm is a fixed cost of the shared evidence stream, identical for all methods, and is published in full per seed (criterion 7). It is never hidden inside or netted against TEST results.

expected_failure_modes: Stationary partial false firing (pre-registered, the cycle's central cost-side risk): a single opposed newest event occurs on stationary evidence at the simulator's flip rates (true stochastic flip 1/8 per non-neutral action plus report flip 1/20) far more often than a full opposed pair, and neither remaining release applies - leg P is designed ARMED on stationary evidence (design purity 0.8375; realized control purity 0.750-0.905 on the purity-only cohorts, armed at all 15 graded control states per cohort) and the carried-over authority arming (NOT stable_disagreement) also holds on stationary arms by design. A stationary partial trigger therefore fires a full 16-task abstention; ONE such state at a control checkpoint where recent8 scores about 7 or more consumes most of criterion 6's successes margin (6), and TWO such states (32/240 abstentions, exactly the budget) are by themselves likely to fail criterion 6(b) unless offset by productive control recovery elsewhere. This outcome is charged against criterion 6, not excused, and the report must state each surviving control state's opposed_count and trigger kind.

Late partial firing at checkpoint 32 (pre-registered): the same widening applies at k=32, where the purity-only candidate held the abstained branch at 0/9 on both cohorts (on additional via an exercised leg-P release). A late partial trigger with realized purity >= 0.70 takes the abstained branch and fails criterion 5(d) (0 of 9) even while sub-conditions (a)-(c) pass. That outcome would show the trigger threshold, not the gate, was also what kept late abstention rare under the full-pair rule, and is charged as recorded.

Engagement still sparse - signal absence, not threshold (pre-registered): B1 states at opposed_count == 0 are unreachable under ANY threshold on this signal (precedents: the single non-taken development return-A k=2 state in the extended-reference cohorts was information-empty under both references; 5 of 6 return-A k=2 states across the long-disagreement cohorts were joint-silent with opposed_count == 0). A cohort drawing 3+ such B1 states of 6 cannot pass criterion 9(a) regardless of widening; the records-only derivations make threshold-vs-absence attribution exact (if the partial-ungated rule also took fewer than 3, the failure is signal absence; if it took >= 3 and the candidate fewer, leg P or authority blocked the difference). Either way criterion 9 is charged, not excused.

Partial engagement without harm conversion (pre-registered): a partial firing at a state where recent8's harm was already low, or where the single opposed event is a flip artifact of the pre-switch rule, removes few harmful actions while forfeiting that state's successes in full. Criterion 9 grades harm (<= guard AND < recent8) jointly with engagement, and B1 successes are reported in full against recent8's, the guard's, and always_abstain's, so an engagement PASS bought by empty abstentions cannot be reported as protection.

Displacement at B2 and return-A onset (bounded, recorded): the widened trigger sits BELOW both recovery branches in the decision order, so it cannot displace a recovery firing; but at B2 / return-A states where neither recovery branch fired, partial abstention now fires where the graded candidates acted through recent8 - changing those states' harm in either direction. That is charged through criteria 1, 4, and 3 unchanged, with partial firings at those stages reported by trigger kind.

Leg P disarming a partial B1 firing on purity noise (pre-registered): checkpoint-4 design purity is 0.8105 and checkpoint-2's is 0.8375, each roughly 1.6-2.0 sd above the 0.70 threshold at about 40 matched reference events, so an onset state can realize purity below 0.70 and lose a partial firing the ungated partial rule would have taken (the purity-only cohorts realized 0 of 12 such B1 disarmings under the full-pair trigger). Recorded per state via abstention_disarmed_by_purity and charged against criterion 9 through lost protection.

Minority-model flip-symmetry limit (carried over, stated): the minority branch this candidate carries exploits this simulator's exact-inversion structure. The widened abstention trigger itself is structure-agnostic (it reads only opposition against reference majorities), but any PASS remains bounded to this inversion simulator: B1 onset protection by a partial-opposition-triggered, purity-gated abstention branch, not a general first-contact solution, not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.

fixed_parameters.abstention_gate: IDENTICAL to the graded abstention-purity-only candidate: the gate on the ABSTENTION branch only has ONE leg - LEG P, the reference-purity gate armed iff reference_purity >= 0.70 (the identical quantity and threshold that bound the recovery branches, UNCHANGED). There is NO support leg (leg S): no acting-window opposed count, supporting count, or any other corroboration quantity is consulted by the gate or by any other branch. The recovery branches, their authority condition, the purity gate as applied to them, the minority branch, the acting model, and every carried-over definition are unchanged. What changes in this experiment is not the gate but the TRIGGER the gate sits on (see abstention_trigger). An abstention trigger whose carried-over arming holds but whose gate leg P is disarmed is recorded (abstention_disarmed_by_purity) and falls through to recent8, exactly as in the graded purity-only candidate.
fixed_parameters.acting_model: A RelationOutcomeMemory (existing estimator: engineered max-minus-min span statistic, 0.25 Laplace smoothing as coded in relation_outcome_memory.py) fitted on the LAST 8 observed public events only - identically the recent8 baseline, exactly as in the graded guard, retained-recovery, joint, bounded, long-disagreement, extended-reference, minority-archive, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates.
fixed_parameters.action_scoring: Whichever model the decision rule selects, the choice is that model's RelationOutcomeMemory.choose output. An abstention is scored as a failed task, never as a success, and is reported separately.
fixed_parameters.archive_concordance_test: IDENTICAL per-event definition to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, the archive expectation is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among ALL archive events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null); e is archive-MATCHED if its expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is archive-CONCORDANT if archive-matched and its reported class EQUALS the expectation. concordant_count and archive_matched_count are in 0..2 and are recorded in full. Raw integer counts only.
fixed_parameters.authority_condition: IDENTICAL to the graded long-disagreement, extended-reference, minority-archive, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned - all three legs, computed from the observed reported stream only, using the same span-majority machinery: (A) LOCAL-ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT (local window = last 26 events; stable_disagreement iff comparable C >= 1 AND disagreeing D satisfies D * 2 > C); (B) ACTING-WINDOW ARCHIVE CONCORDANCE (recent_concordant_count = archive-concordant events among the last 8, in 0..8); (C) PRECEDING-WINDOW ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT (preceding window = 26 events immediately before the local window; preceding_stable_disagreement iff C2 >= 1 AND D2 * 2 > C2; long_disagreement iff stable_disagreement AND preceding_stable_disagreement). BRANCH AUTHORITY for the carried-over branches, unchanged: ABSTENTION armed (before the abstention gate) iff NOT stable_disagreement; RECOVERY armed (before the carried-over purity gate) iff NOT stable_disagreement OR recent_concordant_count >= 2 OR long_disagreement. Would-have-fired disarmed branches are recorded (recovery_would_fire / abstention_would_fire / minority_would_fire) and fall through. The abstention gate in this experiment is an ADDITIONAL condition on the abstention branch only (see abstention_gate); it does not modify any leg of this condition, and this condition does not enter the gate's computation beyond the abstention arming it already supplied. No fitted probability, phase, stage, checkpoint, or elapsed-since-switch count enters either condition.
fixed_parameters.checkpoint: Append-only public events only; record/restore by canonical SHA256 replay exactly as the existing memory classes; restoring must reproduce the full decision record (extended-reference signal records, legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only), archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, the full authority record, the full minority record, the full purity record, AND the full abstention-gate record - per-event acting-window opposition records over the last 8 events (records-only), acting_matched_count, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, support threshold recorded as null, abstention_gate_armed flag, abstention_disarmed_by_purity flag and abstention_disarmed_by_support flag (always false), abstention_trigger_kind (full / partial / none) - all counts, branch taken, acting source) and the choice identically. Maximum 1000 recorded events (existing MAX_SAMPLES).
fixed_parameters.decision_rule: Evaluated in this exact order on every decision once the signals are evaluable: (1) RECOVERY - if joint_count >= 1 AND the recovery branch is armed (carried-over authority) AND the purity gate is armed, act through the recovery model (source recorded as retained_archive), exactly as the graded candidates. (2) MINORITY RECOVERY - else if minority_joint_count >= 1 AND the minority branch is armed (minority_fraction >= 0.25 AND minority_discordant_count >= 8) AND the purity gate is armed, act through the minority model (source recorded as minority_archive), exactly as the graded candidates. (3) ABSTENTION - else if opposed_count >= 1 (partial or full opposition: THE SINGLE CHANGED ELEMENT) AND the abstention branch is armed (carried-over authority) AND the abstention gate is armed (leg P: reference_purity >= 0.70; NO support leg), abstain (choose returns None). (4) RECENT8 - otherwise act through the acting model exactly. A branch whose trigger fires while the branch is disarmed - by its own arming, by the carried-over authority, by the purity gate, or (abstention only) by leg P - is recorded (recovery_would_fire / abstention_would_fire / minority_would_fire, plus recovery_disarmed_by_purity / minority_disarmed_by_purity where purity alone blocked a recovery branch, and abstention_disarmed_by_purity where leg P blocked abstention) and falls through. There is no other input: no stage, phase, rule, or switch information, no acting-window support count, and no fitted probability enters any branch.
fixed_parameters.decision_rule_rationale: Two successive gate generations and then the gate's removal localized B1's failure in sequence: leg S taxed onset triggers with stationary-evidence corroboration (removed last cycle), leg P blocked nothing at B1 (purity armed at all 12 B1 onset states in the purity-only cohorts), and the PRIMARY criterion still failed on additional because the full-pair trigger itself fired at only 1 of 6 states there. The remaining upstream quantity is the trigger's own threshold on the newest pair's information content. A single opposed newest event is weaker evidence than a pair - under the simulator's flip rates it also occurs on stationary evidence - so this cycle does not claim partial opposition is as reliable as full opposition; it tests whether, still behind the carried-over authority arming and the purity leg (both of which were armed at every B1 state and at every graded control state in the purity-only cohorts, so neither is expected to release the new firings), the engagement volume gained at B1 outweighs the stationary and late false-firing volume the same widening buys elsewhere, with both sides graded in their frozen forms (PRIMARY engagement + harm against criteria 6 and 5 unchanged). Keeping every other element identical to the graded purity-only candidate makes the comparison decisive: any difference in outcomes is attributable to the trigger threshold alone, and the records-only purity-only-rule derivation (the graded candidate's exact rule, computable from this candidate's records) states at every graded state what the unwidened trigger would have done.
fixed_parameters.immediate_signal: IDENTICAL to the graded extended-reference, minority-archive, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned: for each of the newest 2 events, a hard span-majority expectation over the 50 events immediately preceding the newest window (indices N-52 .. N-3); strictly-highest reported class wins, tie or empty gives null; an event is matched if expectation and reported class are both progress or damage, and opposed if matched and different; opposed_count in 0..2; no fitted probabilities anywhere. The decision record ALSO carries the legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only, never a decision input), exactly as in the graded candidates, so the graded long candidate's rule remains derivable from the records alone.
fixed_parameters.joint_concordance_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, e is JOINT if it is archive-CONCORDANT AND reference-OPPOSED (extended 50-event reference) on the SAME event. joint_count in 0..2.
fixed_parameters.minimum_events_rule: IDENTICAL to the graded extended-reference, minority-archive, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates: the extended signal (and with it the reference purity, which reads the same 50-event reference window) requires a 2-event newest window and a full 50-event reference window (at least 52 observed events); the archive concordance test requires at least 27. Below 52 events the extended signal and the purity gate (and with it the abstention gate) are not evaluable, reference_purity is recorded as 0 with purity_armed false and the per-event purity records empty, the acting-window opposition records are empty with acting_opposed_count and supporting_opposed_count recorded as 0 and abstention_gate_armed false, joint_count and minority_joint_count are recorded as 0 (their opposed side is not evaluable), and the learner acts with a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on all available events (recorded as not evaluable, gate_evaluable false). Every benchmark checkpoint in this experiment has at least 240 observed events, so all windows are full and the fallback is never exercised during evaluation; it exists only so the class is well-defined for unit tests on short synthetic streams.
fixed_parameters.minority_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded minority-archive, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned. Computed from the retained archive (events[:N-26]) and its own per-span majorities only. For each archive event e: let M(e) be the archive expectation for span(e) under the unchanged archive concordance definition (strictly-highest reported class among archive events of that span; tie or empty gives null). e is ARCHIVE-MATCHED if M(e) is progress or damage AND e's reported class is progress or damage. e is MINORITY (discordant) if archive-matched AND e's reported class DIFFERS from M(e). The MINORITY SET is the set of all minority archive events, in chronological order. minority_matched_count (over the archive) = number of archive-matched archive events; minority_discordant_count = size of the minority set; minority_fraction = minority_discordant_count / minority_matched_count (0 if minority_matched_count == 0). All three counts and the fraction are recorded at every checkpoint.
fixed_parameters.minority_arming: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: the minority branch is ARMED (before the carried-over purity gate) iff minority_fraction >= 0.25 AND minority_discordant_count >= 8. When the branch is not armed it cannot be taken, whatever the minority joint count says; a would-have-fired disarmed minority branch is recorded (minority_would_fire) and falls through. (At B1 onset this arming is expected NOT to hold - realized fractions 0.124-0.192 on the higher-corroboration cohorts - and that non-arming is part of this experiment's limitation evidence, not a parameter to adjust: the minority threshold is NOT changed here.)
fixed_parameters.minority_concordance_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, the MINORITY EXPECTATION for span(e) is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among MINORITY-SET events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null). e is MINORITY-MATCHED if its minority expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is MINORITY-CONCORDANT if minority-matched and its reported class EQUALS the minority expectation. minority_concordant_count and minority_matched_count (over the newest window) are in 0..2 and are recorded in full, with per-event minority records exactly as in the graded candidates.
fixed_parameters.minority_joint_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, e is MINORITY-JOINT if it is MINORITY-CONCORDANT AND reference-OPPOSED (extended 50-event reference, unchanged) - both flags on the SAME event. minority_joint_count in 0..2, recorded in full with per-event minority joint flags.
fixed_parameters.minority_model: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the MINORITY SET events only, with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose).
fixed_parameters.recovery_model: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the retained archive events only (events[:N-26]), with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose).
fixed_parameters.reference_purity_gate: CARRIED OVER IDENTICALLY from the graded reference-purity candidate, unchanged and not re-tuned, and applied to the two RECOVERY branches exactly as graded there. Computed from the extended reference window (the 50 events immediately preceding the newest window, indices N-52 .. N-3 - the SAME window the immediate signal reads) and its own per-span majorities only. For each reference event e: let R(e) be the reference expectation for span(e), i.e. the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among REFERENCE events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null). e is REFERENCE-MATCHED if R(e) is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is REFERENCE-CONCORDANT if reference-matched AND e's reported class EQUALS R(e). reference_matched_count and reference_concordant_count are over the 50 reference events; reference_purity = reference_concordant_count / reference_matched_count (0 if reference_matched_count == 0). The purity gate is ARMED iff reference_purity >= 0.70. Regular recovery fires iff joint_count >= 1 AND the carried-over recovery authority is armed AND the purity gate is armed; minority recovery fires iff minority_joint_count >= 1 AND the minority branch is armed AND the purity gate is armed (and regular recovery did not fire, per the decision order). A recovery trigger blocked by purity alone is recorded (recovery_disarmed_by_purity / minority_disarmed_by_purity) and falls through. In this experiment the same purity quantity and threshold ADDITIONALLY form the sole leg of the abstention gate (see abstention_gate), exactly the role leg P played inside both graded release gates - with leg S removed, not with any quantity re-derived or re-tuned.
fixed_parameters.retained_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: every observed event BEFORE the original reference partition, indices 0 .. N-27, i.e. events[:N-26]. Not phase-segmented, not a snapshot, and receives no phase, stage, or switch information.
fixed_parameters.threshold_justification: Fixed a priori from the simulator's known noise rates, the preceding experiments' published graded aggregates and decision records, and this simulator's published segment geometry, not from any score of this experiment (none exist). (i) TRIGGER THRESHOLD opposed_count >= 1 (THE SINGLE CHANGED ELEMENT): the value is the only widening of a 0..2 count that exists - there is no intermediate threshold to tune - and it is selected by the purity-only grading's own attribution (trigger fired 4/12 B1 states; the remaining states at opposed_count <= 1) together with the guard experiment's published onset distribution (opposed_count == 1 in roughly half of onset states across stages). (ii) ENGAGEMENT FLOOR >= 3 of 6 with >= 1 partial-only firing (criterion 9): the floor is one state above the purity-only protocol's >= 2 floor because the widened trigger strictly contains the old one - a candidate that merely repeats the old trigger's engagement has not tested the hypothesis - and the partial-firing sub-condition prevents a PASS credited entirely to full-pair firings from being reported as evidence for widening (the same not-credited discipline the long-disagreement and extended-reference gradings applied to their null mechanisms). (iii) ALL other thresholds carried unchanged: leg P at reference_purity >= 0.70, minority arming at fraction >= 0.25 AND discordant >= 8, joint tests at count >= 1, authority strict-majority D * 2 > C in both windows, corroboration at recent_concordant_count >= 2 - none re-tuned against any inspected cohort.
fixed_parameters.abstention_trigger: CHANGED from every graded candidate in this line by exactly ONE element: the abstention branch's trigger threshold on the extended-reference signal is opposed_count >= 1 (the newest pair carries AT LEAST ONE matched-and-opposed event - partial OR full opposition) in place of opposed_count == 2 (full pair only). The abstention branch fires iff ALL of the following hold: (i) opposed_count >= 1; (ii) the carried-over abstention authority is armed (NOT stable_disagreement), UNCHANGED; and (iii) LEG P is armed (reference_purity >= 0.70), UNCHANGED and the gate's sole leg. The decision record additionally carries abstention_trigger_kind at every checkpoint: 'full' when opposed_count == 2, 'partial' when opposed_count == 1, 'none' when opposed_count == 0 - a record field only (the branch taken already distinguishes a taken partial firing), included so partial-vs-full attribution is exact from the records alone. No other threshold, window, count, or condition anywhere in the candidate is changed.

expected_failure_modes: Stationary partial false firing (pre-registered, the cycle's central cost-side risk): a single opposed newest event occurs on stationary evidence at the simulator's flip rates (true stochastic flip 1/8 per non-neutral action plus report flip 1/20) far more often than a full opposed pair, and neither remaining release applies - leg P is designed ARMED on stationary evidence (design purity 0.8375; realized control purity 0.750-0.905 on the purity-only cohorts, armed at all 15 graded control states per cohort) and the carried-over authority arming (NOT stable_disagreement) also holds on stationary arms by design. A stationary partial trigger therefore fires a full 16-task abstention; ONE such state at a control checkpoint where recent8 scores about 7 or more consumes most of criterion 6's successes margin (6), and TWO such states (32/240 abstentions, exactly the budget) are by themselves likely to fail criterion 6(b) unless offset by productive control recovery elsewhere. This outcome is charged against criterion 6, not excused, and the report must state each surviving control state's opposed_count and trigger kind.

Late partial firing at checkpoint 32 (pre-registered): the same widening applies at k=32, where the purity-only candidate held the abstained branch at 0/9 on both cohorts (on additional via an exercised leg-P release). A late partial trigger with realized purity >= 0.70 takes the abstained branch and fails criterion 5(d) (0 of 9) even while sub-conditions (a)-(c) pass. That outcome would show the trigger threshold, not the gate, was also what kept late abstention rare under the full-pair rule, and is charged as recorded.

Engagement still sparse - signal absence, not threshold (pre-registered): B1 states at opposed_count == 0 are unreachable under ANY threshold on this signal (precedents: the single non-taken development return-A k=2 state in the extended-reference cohorts was information-empty under both references; 5 of 6 return-A k=2 states across the long-disagreement cohorts were joint-silent with opposed_count == 0). A cohort drawing 3+ such B1 states of 6 cannot pass criterion 9(a) regardless of widening; the records-only derivations make threshold-vs-absence attribution exact (if the partial-ungated rule also took fewer than 3, the failure is signal absence; if it took >= 3 and the candidate fewer, leg P or authority blocked the difference). Either way criterion 9 is charged, not excused.

Partial engagement without harm conversion (pre-registered): a partial firing at a state where recent8's harm was already low, or where the single opposed event is a flip artifact of the pre-switch rule, removes few harmful actions while forfeiting that state's successes in full. Criterion 9 grades harm (<= guard AND < recent8) jointly with engagement, and B1 successes are reported in full against recent8's, the guard's, and always_abstain's, so an engagement PASS bought by empty abstentions cannot be reported as protection.

Displacement at B2 and return-A onset (bounded, recorded): the widened trigger sits BELOW both recovery branches in the decision order, so it cannot displace a recovery firing; but at B2 / return-A states where neither recovery branch fired, partial abstention now fires where the graded candidates acted through recent8 - changing those states' harm in either direction. That is charged through criteria 1, 4, and 3 unchanged, with partial firings at those stages reported by trigger kind.

Leg P disarming a partial B1 firing on purity noise (pre-registered): checkpoint-4 design purity is 0.8105 and checkpoint-2's is 0.8375, each roughly 1.6-2.0 sd above the 0.70 threshold at about 40 matched reference events, so an onset state can realize purity below 0.70 and lose a partial firing the ungated partial rule would have taken (the purity-only cohorts realized 0 of 12 such B1 disarmings under the full-pair trigger). Recorded per state via abstention_disarmed_by_purity and charged against criterion 9 through lost protection.

Minority-model flip-symmetry limit (carried over, stated): the minority branch this candidate carries exploits this simulator's exact-inversion structure. The widened abstention trigger itself is structure-agnostic (it reads only opposition against reference majorities), but any PASS remains bounded to this inversion simulator: B1 onset protection by a partial-opposition-triggered, purity-gated abstention branch, not a general first-contact solution, not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.

hypothesis: The graded purity-only records localize the remaining B1 failure to the trigger's threshold, not to the gate or the branches: (i) leg P blocked zero B1 firings on either purity-only cohort (purity armed at all 12 B1 onset states) and every triggered authority-armed B1 state was taken (4/4 across cohorts), so no gate composition can engage the untriggered states; (ii) at B1 neither recovery branch can protect - regular recovery is archive-blocked at a first switch and the minority branch was unarmed at every B1 onset state on both purity-only cohorts (fractions 0.134-0.185) - so abstention remains the only branch that can move B1 harm; (iii) the untriggered B1 states are not all information-empty: in the graded guard cohorts, opposed_count == 1 was the modal non-triggered onset class (9/18 development and 8/18 additional onset states across stages), so a trigger that also fires on a single opposed newest event - still gated by the carried-over abstention authority and by leg P - should engage at materially more B1 onset states than the 4/12 the full-pair trigger reached, and each such engagement removes that state's recent8-level harm. The priced counter-hypothesis is symmetric and is NOT assumed away: partial opposition also occurs on stationary evidence (a single newest event is opposed under the simulator's flip rates far more often than a full opposed pair), so the widened trigger is expected to fire on the stationary control arm and at checkpoint 32 in a way the full-pair trigger rarely did; whether that false-firing cost stays inside the carried criterion 6 and criterion 5 margins is the experiment's central open question, graded in their frozen forms. If the widened trigger still cannot reach the engagement floor because the remaining B1 states are opposed_count == 0 (information-empty under both thresholds), the failure is signal absence upstream of any trigger, consistent with the two earlier upstream-binding findings in this line (authority age, reference width), and is charged to the PRIMARY criterion, not excused.

simulator.hidden_rules: Hidden physics schedule per seed: A (original progress/damage mapping) -> B1 (progress/damage inverted) -> return_A (original) -> B2 (inverted). Phase boundaries, phase names, and the active rule are benchmark-private and are never supplied to any learner.
simulator.reported_feedback: An independent sha256 draw on (seed, TRAIN episode index) flips a non-neutral TRAIN reported progress/damage label with probability 1/20, exactly as in public_train. simulator.stationary_control_arm: A separate arm per seed with NO rule change: 240 A TRAIN episodes (indices 1000..1239) followed by 64 further A TRAIN episodes (indices 5000..5063, physics original). It measures gate and trigger selectivity when nothing changed - false recovery, false minority engagement, false abstention (now including PARTIAL-trigger false abstention, this cycle's priced risk), lost productivity - and is a co-graded guard population for this experiment (criterion 6): with the trigger widened to opposed_count >= 1, a stationary partial-opposition event that also passes leg P (designed armed on stationary evidence; reference window never mixes segments on this arm, design purity the pure-segment level 0.8375 at every control checkpoint) abstains, exactly the false-firing cost the frozen criterion 6 form prices in advance.
simulator.true_stochastic_feedback: Every actual non-neutral simulator action has probability 1/8 of a progress/damage flip, drawn by deterministic sha256 of (seed, split, episode index, action id, tick) exactly as in StochasticWorld._sample_outcome. Neutral outcomes stay neutral. TEST outcomes are the realized stochastic outcomes, not clean deterministic ones.
